prototype: ad17f54 production code with (deadline, frame slot) instead of deadline-only heap comparisons
notes: All builds emit ACKs but do not apply incoming ACKs or perform runtime recovery. Candidate indexes exact transmit deadlines, unlinks pending frames directly and bounds expiry cleanup to 64 frame views per turn, including prepared batches.

Each build uses identical dependencies, flags and harness on the same kernel. Each sweep retains daemons, TAPs, sockets and private namespaces across 16G, 21G, unlimited and 16G return; PID/start-time checks confirm persistence. No owned build or other test overlaps load.

Directions are L->R and R->L. Daemon, TAP, worker, inner-UDP and process arrays are endpoint L/R. Counter snapshots include drain; process/thread CPU uses the load interval. Receiver samples exclude drain from delivered application-payload goodput.
100% CPU is one CPU. core_cpu includes kernel work on assigned CPUs; softirq is reported separately and must not be added indiscriminately to process CPU for causal attribution.
TAP and socket drops count SKBs, while worker queue-drop events can discard aggregates. Expiry counts frames. These counters cannot be summed into an exact inner loss total.

All observations have zero admission pressure, corrupt/duplicate/out-of-window/wrong-run received records and outer fragmentation. Only prototype index 0 has reordering: 0.000053622955923083124% reverse.

All QinQ super-frame reads concentrate on worker 3 on each endpoint. Left worker 3 also receives substantial outer traffic; right worker 3 receives only control traffic. This verifies concentration, not its full causal cost or a universal CPU ceiling.

One sweep per build is not a five-run acceptance result. Mixed before/after goodput establishes no general throughput gain. Final candidate still declines 2.7% forward under overload; increased socket overflow remains unresolved.
